intents.message: We finished the housing pilot. I need that outcome told three ways — a crisp summary for trustees, a results note for the funding partners, and something warm for the tenants' newsletter — all saying the same thing.
Last month's work on the mobile clinic should reach our medical partners, the county health office and our own volunteers, each with the detail that group cares about and nothing contradicting.
Here are my notes on the quarter. Make a trustee version, a donor version and a staff version, and check none of them overstates the numbers.
The school partnership hit a snag and then recovered. Brief the principal, the parents' association and our funder, each differently, from the same set of facts.
Our board has to decide whether to merge with the other food bank across town. Frame the options, the risks of each, and what you'd recommend.
We could open a second site, deepen services at the first, or partner with the library instead. Lay out those paths honestly and pick one.
Staff are split on moving to a four-day week. Before leadership decides, I want the options, trade-offs and a recommendation with what would change it.
Keep renting our office, buy the building next door, or go fully remote? Give the organisation's leaders a proper decision brief.
Now that three departments use AI tools on their own, where does our organisation stand on oversight, records and risk overall? Score it and tell us what to do first.
For our grant-screening assistant specifically, show a funder how it maps onto the NIST AI framework's functions and where it's weak.
Seniors keep telling us the eligibility scorer ranks them lower. Can we test whether age or disability shifts its results unfairly?
Before we switch on the AI that answers helpline texts at night, write down how we'd catch, contain and own up to a harmful reply.
June's trustee meeting has the budget vote and two declared conflicts on it. Assemble the running order, motions and reading pack.
The Hartwell Trust asked for a three-page proposal for our literacy tutoring. Write it to their priorities and mark every figure I still need to confirm.
Across all our funders — submitted, awaiting a decision, reports owed, stalled — show me the state of play and this week's to-do.
Our foundation wants a light-touch way to gauge how carefully each grantee uses AI with client data, scaled to their size.
An AI scheduling assistant vendor wants access to our clients' calendars. What should a non-technical buyer like me ask before we agree?
The youth choir started under the church's umbrella and now has its own donors. Keep the umbrella arrangement, or incorporate separately?
